    TALLISTON PRESENTS:

    HENRY EVERETT

    STORYTELLING EVENING

    Join storyteller and author Henry Everett in this intimate, enchanting performance exploring the tales of Pan, Robin Goodfellow & more…

    ​

    This intimate spoken-word performance in the round will transport us between the mortal and faerie worlds – and explore our human connection with nature and disconnection from wildness.

    ​

    Spanning tales from Ancient Greece to the realm of Faerie, join us for an enchanting evening of story in the Talliston Watchtower. Under the gaze of our own wild god, Henry will transport us with tales of some of the world’s most infamous tricksters: the Great God Pan and Robin Goodfellow.

     

    ​

    Thursday 21 May 2026

    &

    Mad Spirits

    WILD GODS

    An Unforgettable
    Evening of Story

    THURSDAY 21 MAY 2026
    EVENING FROM 19:00

    Dartmoor-born and based, Henry Everett is a storyteller, photographer, and author of Pixie Folk Tales. He tells traditional tales inspired by our connection to the land, of spirits of place and our human relationship with the magical landscape. These are ancient stories retold for a modern audience, showcasing Henry’s continual quest to explore the places where his imagination meets the world.

    ​

    Full length performance with interval.

    Age advisory 14+

    SOLD OUT!

     “That was insane”

    Michael Dacre, Storyteller

    ​

    “I was so entranced, I forgot to drink my whisky”

    Audience member, Hartland

    THE STORY: Mad Gods & Wild Spirits

    Henry Everett will spirit us to Medieval Britain, for the tales of Robin Goodfellow, aka ‘Puck’. Hobgoblin supreme, famous character of British folk and fairy lore for over five hundred years. His prankster spirit is entangled between human destiny and the song of eternity. 

     

    Then we journey to Ancient Greece for the tales of the Great God Pan. Ancient Greek God of pasture, overlord of wild creatures, and ruler of solitary places… ‘The Great God Pan’ came to embody the spirit of the wild, and one of only a few Greek Gods to have died.

    FOOD & DRINK: Interval refreshments

    The evening's performance will be split into two parts with a half-hour interval allowing for food & refreshments. Your ticket includes a selection of

    light food options, plus hot & cold drinks.

    AFTER THE SHOW: Pixie Folk Tales

    Once the stories are over, there will be time to meet with Henry and take a look at his new book of collected stories – as well as time to relax and explore Talliston's many rooms, each one a story in themselves.

    Click on the book to find out more!
